RequirementText: LILP-REQ-OBJ-001 Each material governance object SHALL possess a stable object identifier within its declared scope.
LILP-REQ-OBJ-002 Each versioned object SHALL identify its version.
LILP-REQ-OBJ-003 Each object relied upon for consequential governance SHALL identify the time or temporal state relevant to its creation or applicability.
LILP-REQ-OBJ-004 Where an object has a predecessor, the predecessor relationship SHALL be explicitly representable.
LILP-REQ-OBJ-005 A material object SHALL be capable of being given a reproducible cryptographic byte identity.
LILP-REQ-OBJ-006 The implementation SHALL declare the hash algorithm used to identify the object's canonical byte representation.

LILP-REQ-OBJ-007 The field containing an object's own final digest SHALL NOT be included recursively within the bytes over which that digest is calculated, unless the implementation defines and proves another non-circular construction.

LILP-REQ-OBJ-008 A required field whose value cannot be established SHALL NOT be silently omitted where omission would conceal uncertainty. The implementation SHALL explicitly represent the relevant condition, including where appropriate: NOT ESTABLISHED NOT APPLICABLE

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-CAN-001 Where cryptographic identity is claimed, the implementation SHALL define a deterministic canonicalisation procedure.
LILP-REQ-CAN-002 Equivalent instances intended to represent the same canonical object SHALL produce the same canonical byte sequence under the declared canonicalisation procedure.

LILP-REQ-CAN-003 Canonicalisation SHALL define all representation details capable of altering byte identity, including where applicable: - field ordering; - character encoding; - line-ending treatment; - whitespace treatment; - number representation; - timestamp representation; - null or absent-field handling; - collection ordering; - and binary encoding.
LILP-REQ-CAN-004 A system SHALL NOT claim reproducible cryptographic identity where its canonicalisation procedure leaves material byte-producing behaviour undefined.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-STATE-001 A consequential determination SHALL reference an identifiable governing state.
LILP-REQ-STATE-002 A Governing State Object SHALL identify the subject, system, actor or other identity to which the state applies.
LILP-REQ-STATE-003 A Governing State Object SHALL identify the authority relied upon or explicitly record that authority is NOT ESTABLISHED.
LILP-REQ-STATE-004 A Governing State Object SHALL identify relevant standing and admissibility where those properties are required by the use case.
LILP-REQ-STATE-005 The evidence relied upon by the governing state SHALL be referenceable without requiring retrospective reconstruction.
LILP-REQ-STATE-006 The policy or rule set governing the contemplated consequence SHALL be identifiable.
LILP-REQ-STATE-007 The scope of the governing state SHALL be explicit.
LILP-REQ-STATE-008 Where jurisdiction affects authority or policy, jurisdiction SHALL be explicitly represented.
LILP-REQ-STATE-009 The temporal context relevant to validity SHALL be explicitly representable.
LILP-REQ-STATE-010 The contemplated effect SHALL be sufficiently identified to determine whether later execution remains within the authorised consequence boundary.
LILP-REQ-STATE-011 A frozen predecessor state SHALL NOT be modified to represent later conditions.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-AUTH-001 Authority SHALL be represented separately from technical capability.
LILP-REQ-AUTH-002 An Authority Object SHALL identify the subject to whom or to which the authority applies.
LILP-REQ-AUTH-003 The authority class SHALL be explicit. Authority classes MAY include, where applicable: OBSERVE INTERPRET PROPOSE DETERMINE GOVERN EXECUTE WITNESS
LILP-REQ-AUTH-004 Authority scope SHALL be bounded.
LILP-REQ-AUTH-005 Where authority is jurisdiction-dependent, the governing jurisdiction SHALL be identifiable.
LILP-REQ-AUTH-006 Where authority has temporal limits, those limits SHALL be representable.

LILP-REQ-AUTH-007 Revocation, expiry, suspension or another material authority-state change SHALL invalidate reliance on the earlier execution authority where that change is relevant to the contemplated effect.
LILP-REQ-AUTH-008 Execution authority SHALL be evaluated at the time required for consequential execution and SHALL NOT be inferred solely from historical authority.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-EVID-001 Each material Evidence Object SHALL possess a stable evidence identifier.
LILP-REQ-EVID-002 The evidence class SHALL be explicit where different epistemic classes could materially affect the determination.
LILP-REQ-EVID-003 Direct observation SHALL remain distinguishable from interpretation.
LILP-REQ-EVID-004 Where interpretation is derived from an observation, the relationship between the interpretation and underlying observation SHALL be inspectable.
LILP-REQ-EVID-005 Where source identity is material to evidentiary weight or authority, the evidence SHALL identify that source or explicitly record that the source identity is NOT ESTABLISHED.
LILP-REQ-EVID-006 Where time affects relevance or validity, the observation or acquisition time SHALL be preserved.
LILP-REQ-EVID-007 Where integrity of an external evidence payload is claimed, the payload or a verifiable content reference SHALL be bound to an integrity identifier.
LILP-REQ-EVID-008 Evidence absence SHALL NOT be represented as evidence of the opposite proposition unless the applicable method independently establishes that inference.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-DELTA-001 A system relying on historical state SHALL be capable of detecting or receiving information about material change relevant to its mandatory governance predicates.
LILP-REQ-DELTA-002 A detected material change SHALL be represented separately from the predecessor state.
LILP-REQ-DELTA-003 The predecessor SHALL remain preserved.
LILP-REQ-DELTA-004 The Delta Object SHALL identify which governing predicates are affected where that relationship can be established.
LILP-REQ-DELTA-005 Where materiality cannot be determined with available evidence, the system SHALL permit a NOT ESTABLISHED result.
LILP-REQ-DELTA-006 A delta affecting a mandatory execution predicate SHALL trigger reassessment before consequential execution.

LILP-REQ-DELTA-007 A system SHALL NOT preserve an earlier ALLOW determination as sufficient execution authority where a subsequent material delta invalidates one or more conditions on which that determination relied.
Notes: Corrected successor extraction; v0.1 predecessor contained following structural content.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-CHAIN-001 Chain continuity SHALL NOT be inferred solely because two objects use the same human-readable name.
LILP-REQ-CHAIN-002 Where identity continuity is required, sufficient identity evidence SHALL exist to support the claimed link.
LILP-REQ-CHAIN-003 Where required continuity cannot be established without inventing or retrospectively constructing missing evidence, the system SHALL NOT claim continuity.
LILP-REQ-CHAIN-004 NEW_CHAIN_REQUIRED SHALL preserve the predecessor chain rather than rewriting it into the successor.
LILP-REQ-CHAIN-005 A chain boundary determination SHALL be recorded where it materially affects execution, verification or claim scope.
Notes: Corrected successor extraction; v0.1 predecessor contained following structural content.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-RCPT-001 Each receipt SHALL have a unique receipt identifier within the declared receipt namespace.
LILP-REQ-RCPT-002 Receipt creation tooling SHALL NOT silently replace an existing receipt under the same receipt identifier.

LILP-REQ-RCPT-003 Where a requested receipt identifier already exists, the implementation SHALL: - refuse the write; - or create an explicitly identified successor or correction object. It SHALL NOT silently overwrite the predecessor.
LILP-REQ-RCPT-004 A receipt SHALL identify when it was recorded.
LILP-REQ-RCPT-005 A receipt SHALL identify the state, event or object to which it refers.
LILP-REQ-RCPT-006 Where a receipt asserts reliance upon a Governing State Object, it SHALL bind to that state by an independently checkable identifier.
LILP-REQ-RCPT-007 Where cryptographic identity is claimed, the receipt SHALL be independently re-hashable using the declared canonicalisation and hash procedure.
LILP-REQ-RCPT-008 Where receipts are cryptographically chained, the predecessor receipt identity SHALL be included in the successor's canonical input.
LILP-REQ-RCPT-009 A correction receipt SHALL preserve the observed deficiency or error rather than representing the corrected state as though the deficiency never occurred.
LILP-REQ-RCPT-010 Execution status and consequence status SHALL remain distinguishable.
Notes: Corrected successor extraction; v0.1 predecessor contained following structural content.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-EXEC-001 Evidence that execution was attempted SHALL NOT be represented as evidence that the intended consequence completed.
LILP-REQ-EXEC-002 Evidence that a consequence occurred SHALL identify the observation or verification method supporting that conclusion.
LILP-REQ-EXEC-003 Where consequence cannot be observed or established, the system SHALL permit NOT_ESTABLISHED rather than manufacturing success.
Notes: Corrected successor extraction; v0.1 predecessor contained following structural content.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-GATE-001 A consequential action SHALL NOT execute unless every mandatory predicate required for that action is established.
LILP-REQ-GATE-002 A mandatory predicate with value NOT ESTABLISHED SHALL fail closed for the contemplated consequence unless a separately authorised escalation path applies.
LILP-REQ-GATE-003 An earlier ALLOW determination SHALL NOT bypass a later failed execution predicate.
LILP-REQ-GATE-004 Where a relevant condition may change between determination and execution, the implementation SHALL provide a time-of-check / time-of-use control appropriate to the declared risk.
LILP-REQ-GATE-005 Where a material governing condition changes after check but before execution, execution SHALL be withheld until reassessment establishes the new governing state.

LILP-REQ-GATE-006 An execution gate SHALL produce or cause preservation of sufficient evidence to establish: - what predicates were evaluated; - what values were observed; - what determination resulted; - whether execution occurred; - and what consequence, if any, was established.
LILP-REQ-GATE-007 Technical capability to bypass the governance gate SHALL NOT constitute permission to bypass it.
LILP-REQ-GATE-008 Where the architecture claims non-bypassable restraint, conformance testing SHALL include an attempted bypass or equivalent falsification test.
Notes: Corrected successor extraction; v0.1 predecessor contained following structural content.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-DET-001 Each determination SHALL be attributable to the governing state and evidence on which it relied.
LILP-REQ-DET-002 ALLOW SHALL mean that the applicable governance determination permits progression within the declared scope. ALLOW SHALL NOT mean that later execution predicates may be skipped.
LILP-REQ-DET-003 HOLD SHALL preserve non-execution while required information, authority, state or evidence remains unresolved.
LILP-REQ-DET-004 DENY SHALL represent an established prohibition within the declared governance scope.

LILP-REQ-DET-005 ESCALATE SHALL identify or reference a separately authorised process. ESCALATE SHALL NOT itself grant execution authority unless the governing policy explicitly establishes that authority.
LILP-REQ-DET-006 NOT ESTABLISHED SHALL remain distinguishable from DENY.
LILP-REQ-DET-007 INVALID SHALL remain distinguishable from NOT ESTABLISHED.
Notes: Corrected successor extraction; v0.1 predecessor contained following structural content.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-CLAIM-001 Every material claim SHALL identify its claim class or otherwise make the claimed property unambiguous.
LILP-REQ-CLAIM-002 A claim SHALL identify the subject to which it applies.
LILP-REQ-CLAIM-003 A claim SHALL identify its applicable scope.
LILP-REQ-CLAIM-004 Where time materially affects validity, the claim SHALL identify its temporal scope.
LILP-REQ-CLAIM-005 A claim SHALL be traceable to the evidence supporting it.
LILP-REQ-CLAIM-006 A claim SHALL NOT silently combine multiple claim classes where the evidence establishes only one of those classes.

LILP-REQ-CLAIM-007 Evidence supporting an integrity claim SHALL NOT, without additional evidence, be represented as establishing: - truth; - authority; - correctness; - safety; - execution; - consequence; - conformance; - or external validation.
LILP-REQ-CLAIM-008 A conformance claim SHALL identify the exact standard version and conformance profile relied upon.
LILP-REQ-CLAIM-009 An external-validation claim SHALL NOT be inferred solely from internal LILP conformance.
Notes: Corrected successor extraction; v0.1 predecessor contained following structural content.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-PROOF-001 Every proof-level claim SHALL identify the bounded property to which the proof level applies.
LILP-REQ-PROOF-002 Proof levels SHALL NOT be used as universal system scores.
LILP-REQ-PROOF-003 PL1 SHALL NOT be described as independent verification.
LILP-REQ-PROOF-004 PL2 SHALL NOT be represented as establishing semantic truth merely because integrity was verified.
LILP-REQ-PROOF-005 PL3 SHALL identify the procedure and evidence used.
LILP-REQ-PROOF-006 PL4 SHALL identify the verifier and declared verification scope.
LILP-REQ-PROOF-007 PL5 SHALL identify the reproduction conditions and result.
LILP-REQ-PROOF-008 Where independence is claimed, material conflicts or relationships capable of affecting that independence SHOULD be disclosed.
LILP-REQ-PROOF-009 Failure to establish a requested proof level SHALL preserve the highest bounded property actually established rather than inflating the claim.
Notes: Corrected successor extraction; v0.1 predecessor contained following structural content.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-CONF-001 Every conformance claim SHALL name the profile being claimed.
LILP-REQ-CONF-002 Every conformance claim SHALL declare the system, component, workflow or artifact scope being evaluated.
LILP-REQ-CONF-003 A profile claim SHALL identify the exact version of this standard.
LILP-REQ-CONF-004 All mandatory requirements applicable to the declared profile and scope SHALL be evaluated.
LILP-REQ-CONF-005 Each mandatory requirement SHALL receive one of the following statuses: PASS FAIL NOT APPLICABLE NOT ESTABLISHED
LILP-REQ-CONF-006 A mandatory requirement with status FAIL prevents a PASS conformance determination for the affected profile.
Notes: Frozen normative wording preserved exactly; prescriptive language does not use SHALL/MUST/SHOULD/MAY.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-CONF-007 A mandatory requirement with status NOT ESTABLISHED prevents a PASS conformance determination unless the requirement itself explicitly permits that state.
Notes: Frozen normative wording preserved exactly; prescriptive language does not use SHALL/MUST/SHOULD/MAY.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-CONF-008 A NOT APPLICABLE status SHALL include the rationale establishing why the requirement does not apply to the declared scope.
LILP-REQ-CONF-009 A profile PASS SHALL NOT be extrapolated beyond the evaluated scope.
LILP-REQ-CONF-010 Conformance to one profile SHALL NOT be represented as conformance to another profile unless the latter profile was separately established.
LILP-REQ-CONF-011 LILP-FULL SHALL NOT be claimed while an applicable mandatory requirement remains FAIL or NOT ESTABLISHED.
LILP-REQ-CONF-012 A conformance determination SHALL be traceable to its requirements matrix and test evidence.
Notes: Corrected successor extraction; v0.1 predecessor contained following structural content.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-CONF-013 The conformance package SHALL preserve the actual failed tests and known deficiencies relevant to the determination.
LILP-REQ-CONF-014 A conformance package SHALL NOT delete a failed result merely because a later successor test passed.
LILP-REQ-CONF-015 Where a successor run corrects a failure, the predecessor result and successor relationship SHALL remain inspectable.
LILP-REQ-CONF-016 The evidence package SHOULD be independently re-hashable.
LILP-REQ-CONF-017 Where reproducibility is claimed, the evidence package SHALL contain or identify the material necessary to perform the claimed reproduction.
Notes: Corrected successor extraction; v0.1 predecessor contained following structural content.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-TEST-001 Every claimed conformance profile SHALL execute all mandatory general falsification tests applicable to that profile and declared scope.
LILP-REQ-TEST-002 Test evidence SHALL preserve the test input, expected result, observed result and determination.
LILP-REQ-TEST-003 A failed mandatory falsification test SHALL prevent PASS for any conformance profile whose claimed property depends upon that test.
LILP-REQ-TEST-004 A test SHALL NOT be marked PASS solely because the test harness completed without error.
LILP-REQ-TEST-005 A test PASS requires the observed behaviour to satisfy the declared expected result.
Notes: Frozen normative wording preserved exactly; prescriptive language does not use SHALL/MUST/SHOULD/MAY.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-TEST-006 Where the test cannot be completed because required conditions or evidence are unavailable, the result SHALL be NOT ESTABLISHED unless another defined result more accurately describes the condition.
LILP-REQ-TEST-007 A later passing successor test SHALL NOT erase the evidence of an earlier failing test.
LILP-REQ-TEST-008 Test scope SHALL be sufficiently explicit to prevent a bounded PASS from being represented as universal validation.
Notes: Corrected successor extraction; v0.1 predecessor contained following structural content.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-CONF-018 PASS SHALL NOT be issued where an applicable mandatory requirement is FAIL.
LILP-REQ-CONF-019 PASS SHALL NOT be issued where an unresolved applicable mandatory requirement remains NOT ESTABLISHED.
LILP-REQ-CONF-020 PASS SHALL NOT be issued where a mandatory falsification test required by the declared profile has not been executed without an established NOT APPLICABLE rationale.
LILP-REQ-CONF-021 The conformance determination SHALL preserve its claim ceiling.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-WORD-001 A self-assessed PASS SHALL identify itself as self-assessed where the claim could otherwise reasonably be understood as independent verification.
LILP-REQ-WORD-002 A LILP conformance result SHALL NOT, by itself, be described as "certified" unless a separately established certification process authorises that wording.
LILP-REQ-WORD-003 LILP conformance SHALL NOT, by itself, be described as ISO-compliant, IEC-compliant, regulator-approved or government-approved.

LILP-REQ-WORD-004 A LILP PASS SHALL NOT, by itself, establish that a system is: - safe; - secure; - lawful; - ethical in every context; - production-ready; - error-free; - immutable; - trustworthy in every context; - or externally certified.
LILP-REQ-WORD-005 Where such additional properties are claimed, each property SHALL have its own supporting evidence and bounded verification method.
LILP-REQ-WORD-006 The standard version SHALL accompany public conformance claims where version differences could materially alter the requirements.
LILP-REQ-WORD-007 The profile SHALL accompany a public conformance claim.
LILP-REQ-WORD-008 Material scope limitations SHALL NOT be omitted from a conformance claim where their omission could cause the claim to be interpreted more broadly than the evidence supports.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-SEC-001 A LILP implementation SHALL identify material trust boundaries relevant to the declared conformance scope.
LILP-REQ-SEC-002 Evidence crossing a material trust boundary SHALL retain sufficient identity or provenance for the receiving process to determine what is and is not established.
LILP-REQ-SEC-003 A system SHALL NOT represent unverified externally supplied content as internally established evidence solely because the content was received through an authenticated channel.
LILP-REQ-SEC-004 Authentication of a source SHALL remain distinguishable from truth of the source's assertion.
LILP-REQ-SEC-005 Where cryptographic signatures are used, the implementation SHALL identify the key, certificate, trust anchor or equivalent verification basis required to verify the signature.
LILP-REQ-SEC-006 Where loss or compromise of a credential or signing key could alter authority, integrity or provenance, that condition SHALL be capable of triggering reassessment.
LILP-REQ-SEC-007 Access-control permission SHALL NOT automatically be treated as governance authority unless that relationship is explicitly established.
LILP-REQ-SEC-008 A cryptographically intact malicious, false or unauthorised object SHALL NOT be represented as trustworthy merely because its integrity check succeeds.
LILP-REQ-SEC-009 Where protected evidence is disclosed for verification, disclosure SHALL remain bounded to the authority and scope of the examination.
LILP-REQ-SEC-010 LILP evidence mechanisms SHOULD preserve confidentiality requirements without destroying the inspectability required by the declared claim.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-VER-001 A verifier SHALL be identifiable where independent verification is claimed.
LILP-REQ-VER-002 The verification record SHALL identify the verifier's declared relationship to the originating party.
LILP-REQ-VER-003 The scope of independent verification SHALL be explicit.
LILP-REQ-VER-004 A verifier SHALL NOT claim independent reproduction where the verifier did not possess the material necessary to perform the claimed reproduction.
LILP-REQ-VER-005 Automated re-execution by the originating implementation SHALL NOT, by itself, constitute independent verification.
LILP-REQ-VER-006 Use of a different AI model or software tool by the same controlling party SHALL NOT, by itself, establish organisational independence.
LILP-REQ-VER-007 A verifier's inability to examine a material dependency SHALL be preserved as a scope limitation or NOT ESTABLISHED condition.
LILP-REQ-VER-008 Independent verification SHALL NOT expand the claim beyond the property actually examined.
Notes: Corrected successor extraction; v0.1 predecessor contained following structural content.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-DEV-001 A known deviation from a mandatory requirement SHALL be recorded.

LILP-REQ-DEV-002 A deviation record SHALL identify: - the affected requirement; - the reason for deviation; - the affected scope; - the approving authority where approval is applicable; - the effective period where time-bounded; - the expected consequence; - and the residual claim limitation.
LILP-REQ-DEV-003 A deviation SHALL NOT silently convert a failed mandatory requirement into PASS.
LILP-REQ-DEV-004 An exception SHALL identify the governing rule that authorises the exception.
LILP-REQ-DEV-005 An exception SHALL NOT create authority beyond the scope granted by the governing exception rule.
LILP-REQ-DEV-006 NOT APPLICABLE SHALL NOT be used as a substitute for: FAIL NOT ESTABLISHED implementation inconvenience missing evidence or unperformed testing.
LILP-REQ-DEV-007 Where an exception or deviation materially changes the basis of a prior conformance claim, the prior claim SHALL be reassessed.
LILP-REQ-DEV-008 Material deviations SHALL be included in the conformance evidence package.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-LIFE-001 A frozen normative artifact SHALL NOT be silently edited.
LILP-REQ-LIFE-002 A material change to a frozen normative artifact SHALL create a new version or successor artifact.
LILP-REQ-LIFE-003 A successor normative artifact SHALL identify its predecessor.
LILP-REQ-LIFE-004 The reason for material successor change SHALL be recorded.
LILP-REQ-LIFE-005 A successor SHALL NOT cause the predecessor's historical hash identity to be represented as though it referred to the successor.
LILP-REQ-LIFE-006 Where a defect is discovered after freeze, the defect SHALL be preserved in the evidence chain.

LILP-REQ-LIFE-007 A post-freeze correction SHALL identify whether it: - changes normative meaning; - changes implementation guidance; - changes only metadata; - changes only presentation; - or does not alter the frozen object itself.
LILP-REQ-LIFE-008 Where a normative change alters conformance requirements, previous conformance claims SHALL remain bounded to the standard version under which they were established.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-MATR-001 Every normative requirement identifier in a claimed profile SHALL be represented in the requirements matrix.
LILP-REQ-MATR-002 Each matrix entry SHALL identify exactly one normative requirement.
LILP-REQ-MATR-003 Each applicable mandatory requirement SHALL have one determination status.
LILP-REQ-MATR-004 A PASS matrix entry SHALL reference sufficient evidence to support the PASS determination.
LILP-REQ-MATR-005 A FAIL matrix entry SHALL preserve the observed failure evidence.
LILP-REQ-MATR-006 A NOT ESTABLISHED matrix entry SHALL identify the evidentiary gap where that gap can be determined.
LILP-REQ-MATR-007 A requirements matrix SHALL NOT omit a mandatory requirement merely because the requirement failed.

RequirementText: LILP-REQ-FREEZE-001 The candidate standard SHALL possess a reproducible SHA-256 identity before freeze.
LILP-REQ-FREEZE-002 The candidate standard byte length SHALL be recorded.
LILP-REQ-FREEZE-003 Every normative requirement identifier SHALL be unique.
LILP-REQ-FREEZE-004 Every mandatory falsification test identifier SHALL be unique.
LILP-REQ-FREEZE-005 All expected normative section headings SHALL be present.
LILP-REQ-FREEZE-006 The final standard SHALL be inspected for embedded PowerShell prompt or continuation-prompt contamination.
LILP-REQ-FREEZE-007 The frozen lexicon binding SHALL continue to identify: ELIAS-LILP-LEX-001 v0.1 SHA-256: 144EFB9CAAB7A0F0537A84704626AC58C5659A0B50F92AA64086B07918E63488
LILP-REQ-FREEZE-008 The founding provenance binding SHALL continue to identify SHA-256: 2754F23DB9E41A2423D4F7749C617A488D76CE4D9C879A5AA70EFB7755D40E43
LILP-REQ-FREEZE-009 A contradiction inspection SHALL be performed over the normative requirements before freeze. Where an unresolved material contradiction is identified, freeze SHALL be withheld.

LILP-REQ-FREEZE-010 A terminology inspection SHALL be performed against the bound frozen lexicon before freeze. Where a material normative term conflicts with the frozen lexicon without an explicit narrower definition in this standard, freeze SHALL be withheld.

LILP-REQ-FREEZE-011 The final candidate SHALL preserve the distinction between: - capability and authority; - observation and interpretation; - attestation and verification; - historical validity and present standing; - determination and execution; - execution and consequence; - FAIL and NOT ESTABLISHED; - predecessor and successor; - integrity and truth; - and self-assessment and independent verification.

LILP-REQ-FREEZE-012 The final candidate SHALL preserve an explicit external-claim boundary preventing internal LILP status from being represented as: - ISO adoption; - IEC adoption; - regulatory approval; - government approval; - independent certification; - or industry-wide adoption.
LILP-REQ-FREEZE-013 Freeze tooling SHALL be collision-protected and SHALL NOT overwrite a previous freeze artifact or receipt.
LILP-REQ-FREEZE-014 The frozen copy SHALL be byte-identical to the verified candidate.

LILP-REQ-FREEZE-015 The freeze receipt SHALL record: - document identifier; - version; - byte length; - hash algorithm; - frozen SHA-256; - relevant predecessor evidence; - verification result; - claim ceiling; - and successor rule.
LILP-REQ-FREEZE-016 A freeze PASS SHALL NOT be declared if any mandatory pre-freeze verification fails.
